packages.label: צַּדִּיק וְאִילָן — הַצַּדִּיק כְּבְחִינַת עֵץ
packages.label_en: The Tzaddik as Tree — the Righteous One as Life-Giving Organism
packages.reason: The Torah's sole teaching rests on a single extended bechina: the tzaddik shares the essential nature of a tree. A tree gives vitality to everything attached to it (branches, bark, leaves) and even to grasses far away by sheltering them from the sun. The tzaddik similarly gives vitality (חִיּוּת) and illumination (הֶאָרָה) to all who are attached to him, and even to those who are spiritually distant, by covering and protecting them. The tree-parts (branches, bark, leaves) are explicitly called a 'bechina' that the tzaddik possesses — they are structural aspects of the same life-distributing organism. The grasses (עֲשָׂבִים) = the distant ones (רְחוֹקִים) share the same nature: apparently-disconnected recipients who are in fact sustained by the central source through the mechanism of sheltering/covering (כִּסּוּי). All these concepts — tzaddik, tree, branches, bark, leaves, distant grasses, vitality, covering — are expressions of one domain: the reach of the tzaddik's life-force beyond his visible sphere of influence.
